purpose: Declared distributions, constraints, screens and the split plan of the synthetic negotiation items (standing order 102, D-707; docs/loop/stages/NEG_SYNTH_PIPELINE.md). Synthetic items are for development sets, the validation set and the pilots only, never the final test. Every name, subject and wording pool below is invented and declared here, never in code (checks 22 and 174).

item.post_cutoff_reason: the synthetic flag carries an invented item; post_cutoff stays the contamination mark of real items
item.terms_text: synthetic item: invented text written by a language model from a sampled structure (D-707); no third-party source, no terms of use apply
item.attribution_text: synthetic, Project Shimmer (D-707); invented parties, agreement and wording
item.source_note: Synthetic item (D-707): invented text written by a language model from a sampled structure; no third-party source. Development, validation and pilot sets only, never the final test.

subjects: a shared early warning system for cross-border floods
the exchange of observation data on retreating glaciers
the reduction of orbital debris from national launches
joint monitoring of smoke from large wildfires
the management of a shared underground water body
common rules for drifting fishing gear recovery
a joint reserve of emergency shelter materials
the protection of deep sea coral areas
shared standards for coastal erosion maps

card_folder.decision: D-716 (Seckin 16 November 2026 23:16): role S's tools read the cards and the session never does; the tool finds a set's card folder from the set name, so the session names no card path
card_folder.root_default_note: unset, the role root is the parent of the code checkout's folder, since role S runs from <role root>/code
card_folder.rule: a set's cards are read from <role root>/work/keys/<set>, one <item id>.card.json each; only a declared set name is accepted; --keys and --card stay for the lead's side and the fixtures

record_kinds.decision: D-711 (Seckin 16 November 2026 20:40): every set holds complete-record items and missing-notes items; a missing-notes item has one party whose notes are not on record, its key answer not_stated, never the persona
record_kinds.rule: the kind alternates with the seed (seed modulo the number of kinds), so every set's draws hold both about half and half

labeller.decision: D-706 item 1: role V's labeller is an open-weight model of a family Shimmer does not use, run on Lambda
labeller.reason: OLMo (AI2): Apache-2.0 weights, not gated, so no Hugging Face token reaches the rented machine (credentials never leave the laptop); its training data is public, so a contamination question can be checked rather than assumed; a family Shimmer runs nowhere (its local agents are Qwen and Phi, its api profile Claude and GPT) and not the generator's (Claude), so the labeller does not favour its own family's text; a 7B instruct model fits an A10. Llama and Gemma both need accepted terms and a token.
labeller.candidates_rule: read live on the instance: the first candidate whose repository exists, is not gated and states Apache-2.0 terms is used; its exact revision is recorded; none resolving refuses the run

generation.decoding_note: recorded as given by role S; the generator runs with no file, shell or web tool

cue.baseline_decision: D-714 (Seckin 16 November 2026 20:54): the label-permutation null rejects a batch; the majority-class figure and flag stay reported beside it as information only

split.rule: Seeds are a base drawn once at run time by role S (seed-base) plus each set's offset range; the base stays in role S's folder and is never shown, so no one outside role S learns which seed went to which set. Each set draws `drawn` seeds and keeps the first `target` items, in seed order, that pass the validator, the deduplication and the labeller; the rest are counted, never used. Ranges never overlap. Each pilot is read once and then joins development (D-671). No synthetic item enters the final test (D-707).

fix_rule.decision: D-789 (Seckin 19 November 2026 14:07): every fix is measured on its own fresh validation and pilot sets, built before the fix is tried and opened only for that check, sizes and look counts recorded; D-806: the negotiation conflict fix (C4, conflict_question compare) first
fix_rule.rule: A set naming `fix` (an upper-case fix id) and `fix_decision` is that fix's own fresh validation or pilot set: drawn from its own seed range like every other set, never a top-up and never topped up, and not counted as the plan's one validation set or one of its pilots. A fix declares at most one validation and one pilot set. Its names match the label pass's set-name form (letters and digits, an underscore, a number). It is read only for its fix's check; afterwards it joins development like every pilot (D-671).
fix_rule.c4: c4val_1: 40 items, 10 of each party structure the scorer reads (D-715 item 1: at least 5 per structure), 30 seeds drawn per structure. c4pilot_1: 24 items, plain draw, the pilot's counts check only (the compare question answered by form, against occurring at all, the declared mass). Both overlap no other set's range.
fix_rule.r3: r2val_1 and r2pilot_1 (D-840, round 2 on bar lines 2, 3 and 5: R3 room_fate and R3b changes_id_echo): the same sizes and draw as c4val_1 and c4pilot_1, offsets 13,000 and 23,000, overlapping no other set's range. Declared only; drawn when the lead starts the generation (NEG_ROUND2_M4_M10.md).

parts_rule.decision: D-843 (Seckin 14:34 and 14:35, 20 November 2026): round 2 (R3 room_fate, R3b changes_id_echo) is read on the D-798 validation set instead of fresh sets; the set is split first into at least four parts balanced by party structure and record kind, by a seeded rule written and frozen before any run; round 2 reads part 1 only, parts 2 and 3 are for rounds 3 and 4, one part is the spare; each part's look is logged in docs/loop/stages/NEG_ITERATION_LOG.md (docs/loop/stages/NEG_ROUND2_D798.md)

uses.spare: spare (never read unless a later decision names it)

parts_rule.rule: Each pool set's `select` keeps every built item no screen dropped (neg_synth.select_all; no target cap). The kept items of the pool are split by neg_synth.split_parts: parts = max(parts_min, pool // target_per_part), the last part the spare; each party structure with n items goes to its first k = min(parts, n // min_per_structure) parts (k = 0: all to the spare), ordered by record kind and then by SHA-256 of '<seed>:<item id>', dealt round-robin from a start that moves on by each structure's count. Each part's digest is the SHA-256 of its sorted item ids joined by newlines. Written and frozen before any run; the parts are computed by role S right after selection, before any label is read by the lead.

strata_rule.decision: D-711 items 2 and 3, D-715 item 1 (Seckin 16 November 2026 22:31), the party-structure instruction of 20:32 and D-732 (18 November 14:06): every set holds enough items of each party structure for the bar to be read per structure
strata_rule.rule: A set declaring `strata` {structure: count} draws each seed inside one structure, (seed // 2) modulo the number of strata in the scorer's structure order, so it is crossed with the record kind (seed modulo 2); two_singles, teams and one_vs_coalition fix the two parties' kinds (one_vs_coalition in a drawn order), three_or_more draws the number from `parties` restricted to three or more and each kind from `coalition_share`. `select` keeps per structure the first `count` items in seed order no screen dropped; a structure never borrows from another. The target is the sum of the counts, and each stratum draws at least two seeds per item it keeps. The seed scheme is unchanged: base + offset + i over the set's own range, fresh seeds that overlap no other set.
strata_rule.tops_up: A set naming `tops_up` adds its kept items to that declared plain set of the same purpose and is not a set of its own (still exactly one validation set). validation_strata tops up validation: S3's validation draw held 51 three_or_more items, 1 two_singles, 1 teams and 0 one_vs_coalition; the scorer needs MIN_ITEMS_PER_STRUCTURE (5) headline items of each structure a set holds (D-715 item 1), and 10 per structure leaves room for the screens' drops.
